facts.claim: The meeting with Rhea on it, set for the twentieth of August, is now listed as a past touch rather than a booking, under Bluebay's events mailbox.
Memory holds no words for that meeting, so nothing on file says what was said or agreed there.
The file has been quiet for about eight days since the meeting, well inside the engine's default quiet window for the contact.
No reply time is measured either way with Rhea: the file holds no mail between her and Arjun.
The engine files Rhea as an admin contact, seen once.
If another week passes with nothing, the file will have been quiet for over two weeks, and with no stop rule nothing says when the contact goes dormant.

inferences.claim: The meeting looks like an event Bluebay organised, with Rhea among those invited, rather than a meeting she set up with Arjun.
If Arjun and Rhea spoke there, more than a week has gone by with nothing written down and no note to her on file.
Waiting costs more each week: the later a note goes, the less it reads as a natural follow-up, and no stop rule marks when it is too late.

facts.claim: The meeting with Kavya on it, set for the twentieth of August, is now listed as a past touch rather than a booking, under Bluebay's events mailbox.
Memory holds no words for that meeting, so nothing on file says what was said or agreed there.
The file has been quiet for about eight days since the meeting, well inside the engine's default quiet window for the contact.
No reply time is measured either way with Kavya: the file holds no mail between her and Arjun.
The engine files Kavya as an admin contact, seen once.
If another week passes with nothing, the file will have been quiet for over two weeks, and with no stop rule nothing says when the contact goes dormant.

inferences.claim: The meeting looks like an event Bluebay organised, with Kavya among those invited, rather than a meeting she set up with Arjun.
If Arjun and Kavya spoke there, more than a week has gone by with nothing written down and no note to her on file.
Waiting costs more each week: the later a note goes, the less it reads as a natural follow-up, and no stop rule marks when it is too late.

hypotheses.proposition: Arjun met Kavya at the event and meant to write to her afterwards.
hypotheses.needs: Arjun's word on whether they spoke and what was said.

hypotheses.proposition: Kavya was on the invitation but they never spoke, so there is nothing to follow up.
A follow-up went to her by a route this file cannot see.
hypotheses.needs: Arjun saying so, or a mailbox shown to have read this file's mail.

unknowns.question: Whether Arjun went to the event and spoke with Kavya.
unknowns.relevance: Without a conversation there is nothing to follow up, and the file can close.

unknowns.question: What, if anything, was said or promised between them.
unknowns.relevance: A promise made there would make a note owed, not optional.

unknowns.question: Who Kavya is and what FerryPay does.
unknowns.relevance: It decides whether the contact serves any goal in the brief, such as design partners or the seed round.

frames.primary: A contact from an event on the calendar, with nothing on file since: if you met Kavya there, the moment for an easy follow-up is passing.
rivals: An invitation list, not a conversation: Kavya was on it, Arjun never spoke with her, and nothing is owed.
A follow-up that went by phone or another mailbox, which this file cannot see.

expected_vs_actual.expected: No playbook applies and the brief names no kind of work for this file; from the file's own shape, a first meeting is followed within days by a short note, or by a decision that none is needed.
expected_vs_actual.actual: The meeting's date passed over a week ago, and nothing has been written in the file since.

scenarios.do_nothing: The contact goes cold, and whatever came of the event is lost.
scenarios.act: Arjun says whether he met Kavya; if he did, a short note this week keeps the contact warm, and if not, the file closes.
scenarios.best: They spoke, Arjun's note lands while the event is still fresh, and Kavya answers with something that serves the brief's goals.
scenarios.worst: Kavya expected a note that never came, and a useful contact is lost for want of a few lines.
signals_to_watch: Arjun's answer on whether they spoke
A note from Arjun to Kavya in the file

reasons: Over a week has passed since the meeting with nothing on file.
Nothing in the file shows what the contact is worth.
A late note is still possible and costs little.

next_move.what: Say whether you spoke with Kavya at the Bluebay event and what was said; if you did, send her a short follow-up note this week.

parsed.alternative: If you did not speak with her, close the file with no note.
parsed.wait_or_stop: Do not wait for Kavya to write first; stop if you did not meet her or nothing came of it.
parsed.done_when: You have said whether you met, and either a note to Kavya is in the file or the file is closed.
